interface.signature: def countOfNodes(graph: List[List[int]], n: int) -> int:

preconditions.description: The number of nodes n must be between 1 and 10^4 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(graph) == n and all(len(neighbors) >= 0 for neighbors in graph)
preconditions.description: The graph is represented as an adjacency list with exactly n entries, each containing a list of neighbors.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= u < n and 0 <= v < n for neighbors in graph for v in neighbors for u in range(n))
preconditions.description: All node indices in the adjacency list are valid (0 ≤ node < n).
The graph is connected and acyclic (tree structure), so there are exactly n-1 edges and no cycles.

postconditions.expression: return_value == sum(1 for u in range(n) for v in range(u + 1, n) if (distance := bfs_distance(graph, u, v)) is not None and distance % 2 == 0)
postconditions.description: The function returns the count of unordered node pairs (u, v) where u < v and the shortest path distance between u and v is even. The distance is computed using BFS.
